observation.visible_scene: A still, fog-shrouded expanse of grey water. An adult white swan floats left of centre with a brown cygnet to its lower left; over the segment additional brown cygnets appear on the right side of the frame. Each bird casts a soft reflection directly beneath it.
visible_changes: The adult swan's neck, held upright at the start, bends forward and then curves back over its body, tucking its head against its back around the middle of the clip and keeping that tucked resting/preening posture until the end.
A brown cygnet enters at the right edge and drifts leftward toward the centre, slowing to a near stop in the right-central area.
A further brown cygnet appears at the far right edge later in the clip and drifts slowly leftward.
The left cygnet drifts gradually leftward while keeping its head raised.

All birds grow progressively smaller in frame while the swan's body also shifts leftward; this uniform shrinkage is consistent with either a camera zoom-out or the birds receding, and the featureless foggy background gives no fixed reference to decide between them.
Reflections of the birds remain visible on the water surface below them throughout.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the size reduction is due to camera zoom or the birds swimming away from the viewpoint.
What preceded the swan's neck-tuck and what follows after the clip ends.
The exact number of cygnets, since some enter/exit at the frame edges.
uncertain_details: Distinguishing camera movement from object movement is unreliable because the background is a uniform haze with no landmarks.
The left cygnet's motion is slow and partly masked by the apparent global scaling.
The right-edge birds are only partially visible at the boundaries of the crop.
